note: Inspect texts for the gathered items (data/items/gathered.json). tools/gen_gathered_items.py merges them in; the first-hour ALWAYS_KNOWN texts in the generator win. Add a line here when a new gathered item appears.

descriptions.acorns: Oak nuts, bitter raw. Soaked and mashed they make a poor but filling food.
descriptions.aloe_gel: Cool clear gel from a split aloe leaf. Soothes burns and sun-reddened skin.
descriptions.amadou: Soft felt peeled from a tinder fungus. Dried, it takes a spark and holds an ember.
descriptions.angelica_roots: A thick aromatic root of angelica. Chewed or steeped as a warming remedy.
descriptions.angelica_stems: Hollow green stems of angelica, sweet and sharp. Eaten fresh or candied.
descriptions.arnica_flowers: Bright yellow mountain daisies. Their salve eases bruises; never eat them.
descriptions.banana_leaves: Broad glossy leaves of the wild banana. Good for wrapping food and shelter roofs.
descriptions.bananas: Short sweet wild bananas, full of seeds. Ripe ones are soft and yellow.
descriptions.beechnuts: Small three-sided beech nuts in prickly husks. Eaten roasted or pressed for oil.
descriptions.belladonna_berries: Shiny black berries of deadly nightshade. Poisonous: do not eat.
descriptions.belladonna_leaves: Dull green leaves of deadly nightshade. Poisonous: a healer's herb at best.
descriptions.birch_bark: Papery white bark that peels in sheets. Burns even when damp; useful as tinder or for containers.
descriptions.blackberries: Dark juicy brambles berries, sweet when fully black. Eaten fresh or cooked.
descriptions.blueberries: Small blue berries from low bushes. Sweet, and they stain the fingers.
descriptions.brinebells: Salt-loving shore flowers that ring like little bells. Chewed, they taste of the sea.
descriptions.burdock_roots: A long dark taproot, earthy and sweet when cooked. Dug from disturbed ground.
descriptions.burrs: Hooked seed heads of burdock that cling to cloth and fur. Pests, and a kind of fastener.
descriptions.cactus_pads: Flat fleshy cactus pads, spines still on. Peeled and cooked they make food and water.
descriptions.chamomile_flowers: Small white daisies with yellow centres. A calming tea.
descriptions.chanterelles: Golden funnel-shaped mushrooms with a fruity smell. A good find in the woods.
descriptions.charcoal_wood: Alder wood fit for burning down to charcoal. Hotter and cleaner than a wood fire.
descriptions.cherries: Small dark wild cherries, tart. Eaten fresh, or pitted and cooked.
descriptions.cherry_wood: Reddish close-grained wood of the wild cherry. Takes a polish; makes fine small work.
descriptions.chestnuts: Glossy brown nuts in spiny husks. Roasted, they are sweet and starchy.
descriptions.cinderfoot_caps: Rust-orange mushroom caps with dark gills, found where old fires burned. Not for eating until identified.
descriptions.cloudberries: Amber northern berries on low bogs. Rare, tart and prized.
descriptions.coconuts: A heavy husked nut with sweet water inside. Crack it open to drink.
descriptions.comfrey_leaves: Rough hairy leaves of comfrey. Bruised and bound on sprains as a poultice.
descriptions.comfrey_roots: A thick black root of comfrey, mucky and slimy inside. Used for poultices; not for eating.
descriptions.crab_apples: Hard sour little apples. Cooked down with honey they are good.
descriptions.cranberries: Tart red berries of the bog. They keep a long time.
descriptions.crowberries: Black berries of low moorland shrubs. Watery and mild; better than nothing.
descriptions.dandelion_flowers: Bright yellow flower heads. Fried or steeped for tea.
descriptions.dandelion_leaves: Bitter toothed leaves. Eaten as a spring salad or boiled.
descriptions.dandelion_roots: A long pale taproot, bitter. Roasted and ground as a coffee, or boiled.
descriptions.dates: Sticky sweet dates from a date palm. They keep well and travel well.
descriptions.drakethorn_berries: Dark red berries on a thorny shrub said to grow where drakes have lain. Handle with care until identified.
descriptions.duskmallow_flowers: Soft violet blooms that open at dusk. Their scent is calming.
descriptions.duskmallow_roots: Pale roots of duskmallow, slimy when boiled. Soothes a sore throat.
descriptions.dye: A pot of plant colour pressed from flowers and roots. Stains cloth and wood.
descriptions.echo_moss: Springy grey-green moss that seems to muffle sound around it. Grows in damp hollows.
descriptions.elderberries: Dark purple berries in drooping clusters. Cooked, they are good; raw they upset the stomach.
descriptions.elderflowers: Creamy lacy flower sprays with a sweet musky smell. Steeped as a cordial.
descriptions.emberroots: Red-brown roots that stay warm to the touch. Said to be good fuel and a hot spice.
descriptions.everember_needles: Needles of the everember tree, dark green and resinous. They smoulder rather than burn.
descriptions.everember_sap: A sticky amber sap that smells of warm spice. Burns slowly.
descriptions.everember_wood: Dense dark wood of the everember, slow to burn and warm to hold.
descriptions.feverfew: Small daisy-like flowers with bitter leaves. A headache remedy.
descriptions.fiddleheads: Tightly curled young fern fronds. Cooked, they taste green and nutty.
descriptions.fine_wood: Well-grown timber chosen for its grain. Makes quality lumber and furniture.
descriptions.fly_agaric_caps: Bright red caps with white flecks. Poisonous: do not eat.
descriptions.fodder: Coarse leaves and twigs that animals will eat. No good for people.
descriptions.food: Plain edible things gathered in the wild. Eat to stay on your feet.
descriptions.foxglove_leaves: Soft downy leaves of foxglove. Poisonous: a heart medicine in the right hands.
descriptions.frostglass_petals: Clear glassy petals of an orchid that grows on the frozen slopes. Brittle and cold to touch.
descriptions.gloaming_star: A pale star-shaped flower that glows faintly at dusk. Picked, it fades by morning.
descriptions.gloomthistle_down: Dark grey thistle fluff, soft and light. Fills pillows and burns quick.
descriptions.gloomthistle_heads: Spiny dark thistle heads. Handle with gloves.
descriptions.greens: Mixed wild leaves, nettle and the like. Boiled they are a plain green food.
descriptions.gum: Sticky tree gum, hardened in lumps. Chewed, or used as glue.
descriptions.hagwillow_bark: Grey twisted bark of the hag willow, bitter. Steeped it eases aches.
descriptions.hagwillow_withies: Springy shoots of the hag willow. Woven into baskets and fences.
descriptions.hard_wood: Heavy dense wood, slow to cut. Makes strong tool handles and posts.
descriptions.hardwood: Heavy timber from broadleaf trees such as oak and beech. Strong, and slow to burn.
descriptions.haws: Small red berries of the hawthorn, mealy and mild. Cooked into jelly.
descriptions.hawthorn_blossom: White spring blossom of the hawthorn, sweet and faintly rank. A mild heart tonic.
descriptions.hazelnuts: Round hard-shelled nuts. Crack and eat; they keep well.
descriptions.hearthwood_logs: Heavy logs of the hearthwood tree, said to burn all night and never spit.
descriptions.heartroots: Red knotted roots shaped like fists. A hardy food and a warming remedy.
descriptions.henbane_leaves: Sticky hairy leaves of henbane. Poisonous: do not eat.
descriptions.henbane_seeds: Tiny grey seeds from a henbane pod. Poisonous: do not eat.
descriptions.herbs: A bundle of mixed wild herbs. Flavours food.
descriptions.honey_flowers: Heather flowers heavy with nectar. Bees love them; so does a good honey.
descriptions.honeyspindle_nectar: A sweet golden nectar drained from honeyspindle flowers. Sweetens any dish.
descriptions.honeyspindle_pods: Slim pods of the honeyspindle, full of sweet seed. Good to chew.
descriptions.hushfern_fronds: Soft grey fronds that deaden footfalls. Grows in quiet ravines.
descriptions.juniper_berries: Dark blue aromatic berries. Flavour meats and ferment drinks.
descriptions.kindling: Thin dry twigs and shavings that catch quickly. The start of any fire.
descriptions.lantern_dew: Glowing drops collected from the dewlantern plant. Faintly lights a dark corner.
descriptions.lavender_flowers: Purple flower spikes with a clean scent. Dried they sweeten linen.
descriptions.lingonberries: Small tart red berries. Keep well and cook well.
descriptions.linseed: Small shiny brown flax seeds, rich in oil. Eaten or pressed.
descriptions.lumencap_caps: Pale mushroom caps that glow softly in the dark. Not for eating until identified.
descriptions.marjoram: A sweet herb with oval leaves. Flavours meat and stews.
descriptions.marrowroots: Fat pale roots as thick as a wrist. Cooked, they are soft and filling.
descriptions.meadowsweet_flowers: Frothy cream flowers smelling of honey and almonds. A mild remedy for aches.
descriptions.mint: Fresh green leaves with a cool sharp scent. Flavours food and tea.
descriptions.mirrorbark_bark: Smooth silver bark that gleams like a mirror in sunlight. Peels in bright sheets.
descriptions.mirrorbark_wood: Fine pale wood from the mirrorbark tree. Takes a bright polish.
descriptions.mirrorcap_caps: Shiny silver-grey mushroom caps. Not for eating until identified.
descriptions.morels: Honeycombed brown mushroom caps found in spring. Eaten cooked, never raw.
descriptions.mournbloom_petals: Dark petals of the mournbloom, grown over old graves. Not for eating.
descriptions.mugwort: Grey-green leaves with a bitter smell. A hardy herb, steeped or burned.
descriptions.nightcrown_blooms: Large pale flowers that open only at night. Scent heavy and sweet.
descriptions.oil: A small jar of pressed plant oil. Cooks, lights lamps and keeps leather supple.
descriptions.owlpetals: Round pale petals marked like eyes. Said to help one see in the dark.
descriptions.palm_fronds: Long woody fronds. Woven into mats and roofs.
descriptions.palm_wood: Fibrous trunk wood of palms. Soft to cut, poor for fuel.
descriptions.pilgrims_cup_pitchers: The cup-shaped leaves of the pilgrim's cup, holding rain. Pick one to drink from.
descriptions.pilgrims_cup_water: Clear rainwater held in a pilgrim's cup leaf. Safe enough to drink.
descriptions.pine_tar: Thick black tar boiled from pine. Seals roofs and soaks wood against rot.
descriptions.plantain_leaves: Broad ribbed leaves of the common plantain. Chewed and applied to stings and cuts.
descriptions.poles: Long straight shoots cut for fencing and frames. Strong and light.
descriptions.porcini: Fat brown-capped mushrooms with a thick pale stem. A fine meal.
descriptions.potash: Grey ash of salt-bush, rich in lye. Used for soap and glass.
descriptions.prickly_pears: Red-purple fruit of the prickly pear, covered in fine spines. Peel before eating.
descriptions.puffball: A round white mushroom the size of a head. Sliced and fried; spoils in a day.
descriptions.quenchbell_heads: Blue bell-shaped flower heads holding a mouthful of sweet water.
descriptions.raspberries: Soft red berries that crumble when picked. Sweet when fully ripe.
descriptions.raspberry_leaves: Toothed leaves of the raspberry cane. Steeped as a soothing tea.
descriptions.resin: Sticky sap from conifers, hardened into amber lumps. Burns hot, seals wood, and sticks things.
descriptions.rimecap_caps: Frost-pale mushroom caps that grow on cold north slopes. Not for eating until identified.
descriptions.riverbraid_stems: Long flexible stems of a river plant, easily plaited into rope and baskets.
descriptions.rose_hips: Bright red seed pods of the wild rose. Tart and full of seeds; boiled into syrup.
descriptions.rose_petals: Soft pink wild rose petals. Scent a room or steep in water.
descriptions.rosemary: A woody herb with narrow needle-like leaves and a strong resinous scent.
descriptions.rowan_berries: Bright orange-red berries in clusters. Bitter raw; fine cooked into jelly.
descriptions.sage: Soft grey-green leaves with a musky scent. Flavours meat and a remedy for sore throats.
descriptions.samphire: Crisp salty green shoots of the shore. Eaten fresh, or pickled.
descriptions.sap: Sweet watery sap tapped from a tree. Boils down to syrup.
descriptions.sea_buckthorn_berries: Bright orange berries on thorny shore bushes. Sour and oily, rich in vitamins.
descriptions.seeds: A handful of plant seeds. Eaten, or sown in a patch.
descriptions.sevenyear_blossoms: Rare white lily blooms, they flower once in seven years. Treasured.
descriptions.sevenyear_bulbs: A pale bulb of the sevenyear lily. Said to wait years for its season.
descriptions.sleetberries: Small blue-white berries that ripen after the first frost. Sharp and sweet.
descriptions.sloes: Small hard blue-black plums of the blackthorn. Very sour; ripe after frost.
descriptions.softwood: Light timber from pine, spruce and fir. Easy to work, fast to burn.
descriptions.sorrel_leaves: Sharp lemony arrow-shaped leaves. Eaten fresh or cooked into soup.
descriptions.spines: Long sharp cactus spines. Used as needles and pins.
descriptions.st_johns_wort: Yellow star flowers with dotted leaves. Steeped for a gentle remedy.
descriptions.staunchmoss: Soft spongy moss that stops bleeding when packed on a wound.
descriptions.stillwater_petals: Pale petals of the stillwater lotus. Float on calm pools.
descriptions.stillwater_seeds: Round seeds of the stillwater lotus. Eaten roasted; keep well.
descriptions.stormreed_stalks: Tough hollow stalks of a reed that sings in a gale. Strong and flexible.
descriptions.strawberries: Small sweet red wild strawberries. Better than any garden berry.
descriptions.sunberries: Warm golden berries that grow in full sun. Sweet and juicy.
descriptions.sunsilver_leaves: Silvery leaves of a vine that catch the sun. Said to be a good tonic.
descriptions.tanglewort_vines: Long wiry vines that snare ankles. Strong cord when stripped and twisted.
descriptions.tannin_bark: Bark rich in tannin. Used for tanning hides.
descriptions.thorny_canes: Long thorny bramble canes. Used for fencing and snares.
descriptions.thorny_wood: Hard dark wood of the blackthorn, covered in thorns. Makes tough tool handles.
descriptions.thyme: A small tough herb with tiny leaves. A fine flavour for meat and fish.
descriptions.tidecrown_pearls: Smooth pearly beads that grow on a tidal plant. Pretty and valued.
descriptions.tideglass_fronds: Clear glassy sea fronds found at the tide line. Brittle; dry to a salt crust.
descriptions.timber: Rough cut trunk wood for building. Squared up it becomes lumber.
descriptions.tinder_fungus: A woody hoof-shaped fungus. Its inner flesh takes a spark.
descriptions.truthsage_leaves: Silver-grey leaves with a clean sharp smell. Said to loosen the tongue.
descriptions.valerian_roots: Strong-smelling pale roots. Steeped to calm the nerves and help sleep.
descriptions.walnut_husks: Green-black husks of the walnut. Stain the hands brown; used as dye.
descriptions.walnuts: Wrinkled walnut kernels in hard shells. Rich and oily; keep well.
descriptions.wardpine_resin: Sweet clean resin of the wardpine, believed to keep ill luck away.
descriptions.wardpine_wood: Straight clean wood of the wardpine, light and strongly scented.
descriptions.water: Plain water, gathered in a container. Drink it or cook with it.
descriptions.watercress: Peppery green leaves from running water. Eaten raw or in soup.
descriptions.whisperfern_fronds: Long fronds that rustle in still air. Said to hear secrets.
descriptions.wild_carrot_roots: Thin pale roots of wild carrot, tough but sweet. Cooked or chewed raw.
descriptions.wild_garlic_bulbs: Small white bulbs with a sharp smell. Flavour any dish.
descriptions.wild_garlic_leaves: Broad green leaves smelling strongly of garlic. Eaten raw or cooked in spring.
descriptions.wild_pears: Small hard pears, gritty and sour. Better cooked.
descriptions.willow_bark: Grey-brown bark of willow, bitter. Steeped it eases pain and fever.
descriptions.wispbloom_heads: Light seed heads that float away at a breath. Drifts on the wind.
descriptions.withies: Long thin willow shoots. Woven into baskets and hurdles.
descriptions.witness_bark: Deep-furrowed bark of the witness tree, said to carry old marks and scars.
descriptions.witness_leaves: Dark leathery leaves of the old witness tree. Not for eating.
descriptions.wolfsbane_roots: Dark turnip-like roots of wolfsbane. Poisonous: do not eat.
descriptions.wood: Plain cut branches and trunk wood. Burns, or is worked into tools and frames.
descriptions.yarrow: Feathery leaves and flat white flower heads. Packed on a wound to slow bleeding.
